goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails passes the original unfiltered guests array instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). Those are the only emails actually added to the booking. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered `guests` input. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which template to send per attendee via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` for matching emails, otherwise `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the caller includes an email that is already an attendee in the input array (possible because the input schema only validates email format), that existing attendee will be misclassified as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the guests-added notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail is set to true on validation failure but never reset to false when the user edits emails afterward, causing the error message to persist after corrections

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, but there is no code that resets it to `false` when the user edits the email fields via `MultiEmail`/`setMultiEmailValue`. The only reset is on the Cancel button (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`), and it is also not cleared on a successful add (onSuccess closes dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but not `isInvalidEmail`). Therefore the error message can persist even after the user corrects the emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The catch block for sendAddGuestsEmails logs an error message without the actual error object, making failures impossible to debug

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block catches an error but discards `err` and only logs a static string. This is directly verifiable in the diff and does make email-send failures harder/impossible to diagnose from logs (and also silently continues).

adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userId || 0 in the organizer findFirstOrThrow query will throw an unhandled error with a confusing message if booking.userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma "record not found"), which is not caught and would bubble up as an internal error rather than a clearer TRPCError like NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST for a booking missing an organizer association.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the addGuests handler/schema/UI and email logic, but it does not show any test files being added or modified. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify the global claim that "no tests exist" for addGuestsHandler, because tests could already exist elsewhere in the repo (outside this diff). This is therefore not a strictly verifiable defect introduced by the diff, but rather a general suggestion about test coverage.
